flashcard_questions.q: A group of lines in a poem separated from other groups by a blank line — the poetic equivalent of a paragraph.
A stanza or group of four lines, often with a regular rhyme scheme such as ABAB or ABCB.
The continuation of a sentence or phrase beyond the end of a line of poetry, without a pause, creating flow or momentum.

flashcard_questions.a: A pause or break within a line of poetry, usually indicated by punctuation such as a full stop, comma, dash, or semicolon.
A pattern of sounds created by the endings of words at the end of lines — common schemes include ABAB (alternate rhyme), AABB (couplets), and ABCB.
